## Current completion and the conditions of further activity

The [continuing-dependency study](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/CONTINUING-DEPENDENCY-INTEGRATION.md) first asks what further activity actually requires. The existing material law permits both copying through local support and copying through common fuel. Capture therefore cannot be prescribed as generally necessary for reconstruction. Exact least-common-fuel requirements retain both alternatives, including damaged configurations where current copying needs no repair. The target is independently stated as a count increase preserving the active resident and H; it does not silently include every future capacity.

The same original formation history supplies a sharper distinction. After actual losses, local capture followed by copying and direct bulk copying each restore the lost A. Both reached states have an active resident, intact site, empty local store, equal A/H counts and total energy 216. One retains common fuel 1 and source 215; the other retains common fuel 0 and source 216. Under the same subsequent damage, the former can repair. No native event can restore common fuel in the latter, so its failure cannot be dismissed as overlooking another repair sequence. Present completion remains real; the difference concerns the further activity each completed history permits.

The analytical separation of count, energy and support location preserves different aspects of this one history. A summary using only the first two omits a relation needed for the declared repair continuation. The general core already permits preserving it; the branch identifies what this particular abstraction must retain. Neither the resource compartments nor an analyst's target become universally independent primitives. Requiring the later repair is an explicit continuation contract, not an unlimited duty to preserve every possible future operation.

[Twenty isolated Lean audits and independent finite checks](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/CONTINUING-DEPENDENCY-REVIEW.md) establish the general necessary bound, the concrete continuation contrast and agreement across 4,800 configurations. General constructive sufficiency remains a hand proof. The proof uses disclosed `propext`/`Quot.sound` dependencies; the local event law remains supplied. These results neither implement learning nor meet the stronger no-assumptions objective.

The next [material acquisition connection](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/CONTINUING-DEPENDENCY-IDENTIFICATION.md) must make native consequences form retained distinctions and make their use change actual continuation. A recorder with a different source-to-common replenishment law would change the dependency being learned. Its parts and operations must also remain within the history's actual conditions; at the one-common-unit endpoint a newly inserted operation consuming one common unit would consume the repair reserve. Existing learning and inquiry-revision results remain credited, while this composition is unresolved. The [whole-process account](UNIFIED-ETHICAL-GROUNDING.md#the-whole-as-the-grounding-question) separately investigates warranted concern: preserving this synthetic count or capacity alone cannot establish goodness.

## Continuing dependency before its acquisition

The separate [continuing-dependency analysis](continuing-dependency/README.md)
characterizes native reconstruction requirements while preserving this recorder's
original results. Equal present restoration and aggregate energy can leave
different future repair capacity under the original material law. That study
identifies what a future record/action connection must preserve; it does not
import this recorder's replenishment kernel, install new memory or claim the
native dependency has already been learned.
